summary: Computes an amplitude or power envelope around input samples using exponential decay or local maximum window methods.

key_params.name: method
key_params.note: Envelope algorithm: exponential decay or local maximum window

key_params.name: bounds
key_params.note: Magnitude, signal power, maximum, or minimum envelope bounds

key_params.name: width
key_params.note: Window width for local maximum envelope

key_params.name: widthunit
key_params.note: Samples, frames, or seconds for width

key_params.name: norm
key_params.note: Normalize power envelope while adjusting width

key_params.name: samplerate
key_params.note: Sample rate used when Resample Envelope is on

key_concepts: Outputs an envelope from nearby input samples, commonly tracking amplitude or power around each sample.
Type selects Exponential Decay or Local Maximum Window, with different smoothness and enclosure tradeoffs.
Envelope Bounds chooses magnitude, signal power, maximum-value, or minimum-value analysis behavior.
Envelope Width and Width Unit define the local window size used for feature capture.
Interpolate controls how local maximum points are connected into the envelope.
Normalize Power Envelope and Resample Envelope can keep power behavior stable or change the output sample rate.
common_gotchas: Exponential Decay always encloses data but can have discontinuous-looking slopes.
Local Maximum Window produces smoother shapes but signals can jump outside the envelope and pulses can be off by up to half the window.
Large envelope widths smooth more aggressively but add latency and hide fast transients.
For loudness leveling, divide the original signal by a wide envelope with Math CHOP rather than replacing the original signal.
Resampling changes output rate and can affect downstream timing.
